name: Labetalol
executiveSummary: α/β blocker. Adult crisis: bolus **10–20 mg IV** over 2 min, then **20–80 mg every 10 min** (max cumulative **300 mg**) or infusion **0.5–2 mg/min**. Pediatrics: load **0.2–1 mg/kg** (max **40 mg**/bolus); infusion **0.25–3 mg/kg/h**.
indications:
## Indications

- Hypertensive urgencies/emergencies (incl. preeclampsia/eclampsia in obstetric regimens).
- Perioperative BP control when indicated.

## Precautions

- Avoid/extreme caution in asthma/COPD, bradycardia, AV block, decompensated HF.
- Reduce ~50% in hepatic failure. Little renal adjustment.
- May mask hypoglycemia.

> Semi-upright patient; monitor BP and HR with each bolus.

adulto.dose: Crisis: **10–20 mg IV** over ≥2 min; repeat **20–80 mg every 10 min** until control (max cumulative **300 mg**). Infusion: **0.5–2 mg/min** (some protocols up to **10 mg/min** briefly). PO maintenance per label.
adulto.administration: Slow IV or infusion in NS/D5W (e.g. 1 mg/mL). May use undiluted if fluid-restricted.
adulto.notes: Do not abruptly stop chronic β-blockade in coronary patients.

pediatrico.dose: Crisis: bolus **0.2–1 mg/kg** over 2–3 min (max **40 mg**/dose; rate ≤**2 mg/min**); repeat q10 min up to **3–4 mg/kg** or **300 mg** cumulative. Continuous infusion: **0.25–3 mg/kg/h** (neonates: start ~**0.5 mg/kg/h**).
pediatrico.administration: IV bolus or pump; diluent NS/D5W.

stability:
## Stability

- Infusion dilution: ~24 h room temp. Prefer fresh preparation.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypotension, bradycardia, bronchospasm, dizziness, nausea; rare hepatotoxicity; occasional hyperK.
